en.title: The Design of Everyday Things
en.summary: 即使是最聪明的人，也会因找不到正确的开关或烤箱燃烧器、不知道该推拉还是滑动门而感到束手无策。这本极具洞察力的著作指出，这些问题并非源于我们自身的无能，而是产品设计忽视了用户需求与认知心理学原理的结果。从模糊隐蔽的控制界面，到控制与功能之间缺乏逻辑关联，再到缺乏反馈与帮助提示，以及对记忆力的不合理要求——《日常事物的设计》揭示了优秀易用设计的法则：使操作可见、利用功能与控制的自然关联、合理运用约束条件。目标是让用户在正确的时间、正确的界面上，毫不费力地完成正确操作。在这本趣味盎然又见解深刻的分析中，认知科学家唐纳德·A·诺曼将卓越设计视为重获影响消费者行为竞争优势的关键。本书现已全面扩充与更新，并附有作者撰写的新序言，是一本强有力的入门读物，解析为何有些产品能让用户满意，而另一些则徒增烦恼。
en.summaryOriginal: Even the smartest among us can feel inept as we fail to figure out which light switch or oven burner to turn on, or whether to push, pull, or slide a door. The fault, argues this ingenious—even liberating—book, lies not in ourselves, but in product design that ignores the needs of users and the principles of cognitive psychology. The problems range from ambiguous and hidden controls to arbitrary relationships between controls and functions, coupled with a lack of feedback or other assistance and unreasonable demands on memorization. The Design of Everyday Things shows that good, usable design is possible. The rules are simple: make things visible, exploit natural relationships that couple function and control, and make intelligent use of constraints. The goal: guide the user effortlessly to the right action on the right control at the right time. In this entertaining and insightful analysis, cognitive scientist Donald A. Norman hails excellence of design as the most important key to regaining the competitive edge in influencing consumer behavior. Now fully expanded and updated, with a new introduction by the author, The Design of Everyday Things is a powerful primer on how—and why—some products satisfy customers while others only frustrate them.

recommendations.scoreReason: 嘉宾明确推荐或表达强烈喜爱
recommendations.quoteEn: I think the one book that I recommend the most is The Design of Everyday Things by Don Norman. I read it originally in college for an HCI class I was taking, and I think of everything I've ever read, it's the thing that caused me to see the world from the perspective of everything you interact with as a product. Every pencil that you use, every door that you open is a product that somebody designed.
recommendations.quoteZh: 这是这本书的主要启示吗？因为它被提及很多次，而且已经出版很久了。所以对于没读过或没时间读的人来说，这就是你最重要的收获。一切都是有人设计的，而且总有改进的空间。
recommendations.questionEn: Okay, let's do it. Okay, first question. What are two or three books that you have recommended most to other people?

recommendations.scoreReason: 嘉宾明确推荐或表达强烈喜爱
recommendations.quoteEn: …changed the way I think about things. It taught me a lot about a discipline I had never really thought much about, but also because I think it makes me sound smart and it's a really short book, so it's easy to get through is The Design Of Everyday Things. For me, that was the first time that I realized that design wasn't just this sort of cool thing that some people were into and they had to get and it made things beautiful. It was about understanding how everything is designed and how to think about design and usability. (01:21:28): So for someone like me who didn't have any experience in product before, I think it could be transformative. And then the second book, it has nothing to do with what we do. I recommend Viktor Frankl's Man's Search For…
recommendations.quoteZh: 有一本书我推荐得最多，因为它真的改变了我的思维方式。它让我对一个我从未深入思考过的学科有了很多了解，同时也因为我觉得它让我听起来很聪明，而且这本书很短，很容易读完，那就是《设计心理学》。对我来说，这是我第一次意识到设计不只是某些人感兴趣的酷炫事物，它能让事物变得美观。它关乎理解一切事物是如何被设计的，以及如何思考设计和可用性。（01:21:28）所以对于像我这样之前没有产品经验的人来说，它可以带来变革。然后第二本书，与我们所从事的行业无关。我推荐维克多·弗兰克尔的《活出生命的意义》，因为我本质上是个哲学家，我经常思考生命、生命的意义，以及不同生命的区别，以及如何过上美好的生活。无论我们选择何种职业，这一点始终很重要。所以这些就是我的推荐。
